title: Heidelberg Materials — Grokipedia
content: Heidelberg Materials AG is a German multinational corporation headquartered in Heidelberg that manufactures building materials, including cement, aggregates, ready-mixed concrete, and asphalt.](#ref-1) Founded in 1873 by Johann Philipp Schifferdecker as a Portland cement factory employing 35 workers, the company has expanded through acquisitions and innovation to become one of the world's largest integrated producers in the sector.](#ref-2) It operates approximately 3,000 sites across more than 50 countries, employing over 51,000 people.](#ref-1) The firm, formerly known as HeidelbergCement until its rebranding in 2023 to emphasize a broader portfolio of sustainable and digital solutions beyond traditional cement production, maintains leading market positions in its core products.](#ref-3) Its operations span Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, and other regions, with significant production capacities in gray and white cement, slag cement, and related materials.](#ref-4) Heidelberg Materials has pursued sustainability initiatives, such as developing low-carbon cement alternatives and carbon capture technologies, amid industry-wide scrutiny over the sector's substantial greenhouse gas emissions from clinker production.](#ref-5) Key achievements include its centennial-plus legacy of technological advancements in cement manufacturing and strategic expansions, such as the acquisition of Italcementi, which bolstered its global footprint.](#ref-2) While the company reports robust financial performance, with recent annual revenues exceeding €20 billion, it faces ongoing challenges from regulatory pressures on emissions and competition in commoditized markets.](#ref-6).

title: 150 years of progress
content: Factory building with smoking chimneys on a river. Portrait of a man with a sideburns beard. In 1873, Johann Philipp Schifferdecker started producing Portland cement – then a completely new building material – with just 35-employees in Heidelberg, Germany. He probably never imagined that 150 years later, Heidelberg Materials would be one of the world’s largest manufacturers of building materials, with around 51,000 employees in more than 50 countries across the globe (as of 2023). We owe it to our pursuit of progress and our focus on what we do best: building materials. This helped us to turn cement from an expensive material of varying quality to an affordable and high-performing product that has shaped our modern world. For Schifferdecker, the mill is the ideal location for his cement factory. Just over a year after the founding of the company, the young cement chemist Friedrich Schott from Braunschweig is hired on as technical operations supervisor.
